accepted.question_text: When N > 4 and the positive parameters a and b satisfy a^((N-4)/2) b < C1(N), do the conclusions of Theorem 1.1 still hold? In other words, for each sufficiently large lambda > 0 and each convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H1_0(Omega), does there exist some v* in C such that the associated Kirchhoff problem has at least three weak solutions, two of which are global minima in H1_0(Omega) of the corresponding energy functional?

evidence.quote: (B) If a^{(N-4)/2} b > C2(N), then, for each lambda > 0 large enough and for each convex set C subset of L2(Omega) whose closure in L2(Omega) contains H1_0(Omega), there exists v* in C such that the problem (Plambda) has at least three weak solutions, two of which are global minima in H1_0(Omega) of the energy functional defined in (A).
It remains an open question if, when N > 4, Theorem 1.1 holds for every a >= 0, b > 0 with a^{(N-4)/2} b < C1(N).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 1.1. Does the conclusion of Proposition 1 hold if N > 4 and p = 2⋆?

evidence.quote: The paper is motivated by a recent work of Ricceri where the author studied problem (Plambda) in the subcritical case, i.e. when |u|^{2⋆-2}u is replaced by |u|^{p-2}u with p < 2⋆.
In [21, Proposition 1], the existence of two global minima for the energy functional (and three solutions for the associated Kirchhoff problem) is obtained for every a >= 0 and b > 0.
In the same paper, the following challenging question was raised (see [21, Problem 1]): Question 1.1. Does the conclusion of Proposition 1 hold if N > 4 and p = 2⋆?
